title: Share Trading Policy

tiers.name: Orora Person
tiers.description: Employees of the Orora Group (full time, part time or casual), contractors and employees of incorporated contractors, Senior Executives, Directors, and Associates of Senior Executives and Directors.

tiers.name: Designated Person
tiers.description: Senior Executives, Directors, their Associates, and any other person designated as such by the Company Secretary from time to time (and that person's Associates). Includes all of Orora's key management personnel. Subject to additional restrictions: pre-trade notification, and bans on short selling, short-term trading and margin lending/secured financing.

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: Non-executive and executive directors of Orora Limited, including the Chairman of the Board; subject to a duty to notify the Chairman of the Board and the ASX of any change to notifiable interests in Orora Securities.

tiers.name: Chairman of the Board
tiers.description: The Chairman of the Board; distinguished for the recipient of pre-trade notification (the Chairman of the Audit & Compliance Committee, copied to the Company Secretary) and as the default approver of exceptional-circumstances applications by other Designated Persons.

tiers.name: Directors (except Chairman)
tiers.description: Directors other than the Chairman of the Board; must notify the Chairman of the Board, with a copy to the Company Secretary, before trading.

tiers.name: Senior Executives (except MD&CEO)
tiers.description: The Managing Director & Chief Executive Officer's direct reports, other than the MD&CEO; must notify the Managing Director & Chief Executive Officer, with a copy to the Company Secretary, before trading.

tiers.name: Associates
tiers.description: A person acting in concert with, or over whom there is investment control or influence by, an Orora Person or Designated Person; examples include spouses/partners, family members, nominees, trusts and companies controlled by the person or their family.

definitions.hedging_definition: hedging arrangements (including, for example, the use of certain Derivatives)

windows.start_anchor: close of trading on 31 December each year
windows.end_anchor: the day of the announcement to the ASX of the Company's half year results (usually the third week of February)

windows.start_anchor: close of trading on 30 June each year
windows.end_anchor: the day of the announcement of the Company's full year results (usually the third week of August)

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board may decide, from time to time, to impose ad hoc trading restrictions outside Blackout Periods on specific Orora Persons or a class of Orora Persons. Due to the sensitive nature of the underlying activity or knowledge, it is unlikely details will be communicated to all Orora Persons; the Board communicates directly with those subject to the restriction and any such communication is to be treated as confidential.

rules.section: Definitions (Derivatives, Securities); Designated Persons - Notification of Trade
rules.detail: Securities includes Derivatives, expressly defined (per the Corporations Act) to include put/call options, exchange traded options, forward contracts, futures, warrants, structured financial products, swaps, contracts for difference, spread bets and caps and collars, with no venue limitation. Designated Persons must notify the relevant person (Chairman of Audit & Compliance Committee, Chairman of the Board, or MD&CEO, as applicable, copied to the Company Secretary) before Trading, and must avoid Blackout Periods, ad hoc restrictions and possession of inside information.
rules.evidence: 'Derivatives' has the meaning given in the Corporations Act, and includes the following if they relate to or derive value from Orora Securities: put or call options, exchange traded options, forward contracts, futures, warrants, depository receipts, structured financial products, swaps, contracts for difference, spread bets and caps and collars.

rules.detail: Absolute ban on hedging arrangements over unvested Orora Securities issued under any employee share, option or rights plan, applicable to all Orora Persons (broader than just Designated Persons); no clearance route.
rules.evidence: All Orora Persons must not engage in hedging arrangements (including, for example, the use of certain Derivatives) over unvested Orora Securities issued pursuant to any employee share, option or rights plan.

rules.detail: Hedging vested Orora Securities is expressly permitted but must comply with the Policy generally (notification for Designated Persons, no Blackout Period, no inside information) and, if applicable to that Orora Person, Orora's separate Minimum Shareholding Policy, which may cap the amount that can be hedged.
rules.evidence: In addition, any hedging over vested Orora Securities must comply with this Policy and, if applicable to that Orora Person, Orora's Minimum Shareholding Policy (a copy of which is available on Orora's website).

rules.detail: Monetisation structures such as a prepaid forward are not named; they are caught as Trading (transferring the beneficial or legal interest in Securities, or a Derivative deriving value from Securities), requiring pre-trade notification and confined outside Blackout Periods.
rules.evidence: 'Trade' and 'Trading' includes subscribing for, buying, selling or otherwise transferring the beneficial or legal interest in Securities of Orora.

rules.detail: Blanket ban on short selling of any Orora Securities by Designated Persons, with no clearance route.
rules.evidence: Designated Persons must not engage in short selling of any Orora Securities.

rules.detail: The short selling ban is expressed to apply to Designated Persons only; the Policy does not separately address short selling by other Orora Persons.

Securities lending (lending out Securities one holds) is not addressed; the short selling section discusses borrowing a Security to sell short, which is a different concept from lending Orora Securities to a third party.
Contracts for difference are expressly named as a Derivative deriving value from Orora Securities, requiring pre-trade notification and compliance with Blackout Periods.
rules.evidence: 'Derivatives' has the meaning given in the Corporations Act, and includes the following if they relate to or derive value from Orora Securities: ... contracts for difference, spread bets and caps and collars.

rules.detail: Blanket, unconditional ban on margin lending arrangements over Orora Securities for Designated Persons, with no clearance route or security-state carve-out.
rules.evidence: Designated Persons must not engage in margin lending or other secured financing arrangements over Orora Securities.

rules.detail: The margin lending ban is expressed to apply to Designated Persons only; the Policy does not separately address margin lending by other Orora Persons.
The ban on 'other secured financing arrangements over Orora Securities' extends to granting a charge, lien or pledge over Orora Securities generally, not just margin loans specifically.
rules.evidence: Designated Persons must not engage in margin lending or other secured financing arrangements over Orora Securities.

rules.detail: Any secured financing arrangement over Orora Securities, not just margin lending, is banned outright for Designated Persons, with no exemption authority. This is the central obstacle to the loan leg of a funded collar.
rules.evidence: Designated Persons must not engage in margin lending or other secured financing arrangements over Orora Securities.

rules.detail: Ban on purchasing with intention to sell within 3 months, selling with intention to buy within 3 months, and entering short-term arrangements such as forward contracts; carved out for securities acquired under employee incentive plans.
rules.evidence: Purchasing Orora Securities with the intention of disposing of or selling Orora Securities within a three month period; Disposing of or selling Orora Securities with the intention of purchasing Orora Securities within a three month period; and/or Entering into short-term arrangements (such as forward contracts) in relation to Orora Securities.

rules.detail: The short-term trading ban is expressed to apply to Designated Persons only; the Policy does not separately address short-term trading by other Orora Persons.

clearance.post_trade_to: Company Secretary (who provides notification to the Chairman of the Board and the ASX)
clearance.post_trade_deadline: no later than two business days from the date the change occurred
clearance.section: Designated Persons - Notification of Trade; ASX Notification by Directors
clearance.evidence: Chairman of the Board, or their Associates: Chairman of the Audit & Compliance Committee, with a copy to the Company Secretary.

clearance.post_trade_to: Company Secretary (who provides notification to the Chairman of the Board and the ASX)
clearance.post_trade_deadline: no later than two business days from the date the change occurred
clearance.section: Designated Persons - Notification of Trade; ASX Notification by Directors
clearance.evidence: Directors (except for the Chairman of the Board), or their Associates: Chairman of the Board, with a copy to the Company Secretary.
Senior Executives (except for the Managing Director & Chief Executive Officer), or their Associates: Managing Director & Chief Executive Officer, with a copy to the Company Secretary.

short_term.basis: from acquisition or disposal (applies in both directions)
carve_outs: Orora Securities acquired as a result of the exercise of an option (or similar right) under Orora's employee incentive plans
Orora shares acquired under Orora's employee incentive plans
short_term.evidence: Purchasing Orora Securities with the intention of disposing of or selling Orora Securities within a three month period; Disposing of or selling Orora Securities with the intention of purchasing Orora Securities within a three month period; and/or Entering into short-term arrangements (such as forward contracts) in relation to Orora Securities.

exceptions.approver: the Company Secretary, or the Chairman of the Board where applicable
exceptions.evidence: The Designated Person or their Associate will be in severe financial hardship if they cannot Trade in the Orora Securities

exceptions.approver: the Company Secretary, or the Chairman of the Board where applicable
exceptions.evidence: The Designated Person or their Associate are required by a court order to transfer or sell the Orora Securities

exceptions.approver: the Chairman of the Board, or the Chairman of the Audit & Compliance Committee where the Chairman of the Board is seeking approval
exceptions.evidence: The circumstance has been deemed exceptional by the Chairman of the Board or, where the Chairman of the Board is seeking approval, the Chairman of the Audit & Compliance Committee.
Transfers of Orora Securities already held by Orora Persons into a superannuation fund or other saving scheme in which the Orora Person is a beneficiary

Where the Orora Person is a trustee, Trading in Orora Securities by that trust provided that the Orora Person is not a beneficiary of the trust and any decision to Trade during a Blackout Period or other ad hoc restriction period is taken by the other trustees or by the investment managers independent of the Orora Person
Undertakings to accept, or the acceptance of, a takeover offer or scheme of arrangement

Trading under an offer or invitation made to all or most of the Orora Security holders, such as, a rights issue, a security purchase plan, a dividend or distribution reinvestment plan or an equal access buy back, where the plan that determines the timing and structure of the offer has been approved by the Orora Board.
A disposal of Orora Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights

An acquisition of Orora Securities issued under an employee incentive plan provided that where Securities granted under that plan cease to be held under the terms of the plan, any subsequent Trading of those Orora Securities must be in accordance with this Policy
Trading in Orora Securities in a managed securities portfolio where the Orora Person is not in a position to influence the portfolio investments.

exceptions.approver: the Board (standing exception; no case-by-case approval needed unless the employee is a Designated Person, who must still notify)
exceptions.evidence: If a tax liability arises immediately upon awards which vest during a Blackout Period, the employee may Trade the awards received in the period of 4 weeks immediately after the awards have vested in order to meet the tax liability.

financing.minimum_shareholding_requirement: Orora's Minimum Shareholding Policy (a separate document) applies to hedging of vested Orora Securities where applicable to the Orora Person; this Policy does not state whether hedged shares are excluded from the minimum shareholding calculation.

external_documents: Other applicable Orora policies or procedures referenced in relation to the Other Prohibitions in section 9
exemption_authority: For Designated Persons, the Company Secretary (or the Chairman of the Board, or the Chairman of the Audit & Compliance Committee where the Chairman is the applicant) may approve trading to dispose of Orora Securities during a Blackout Period or ad hoc restriction period only for severe financial hardship, a court order requiring transfer or sale, or a circumstance deemed exceptional by the Chairman (or the Chair of the Audit & Compliance Committee if the Chairman is the applicant), provided the person is not in possession of inside information and the proposed trading is the only reasonable course of action; the decision is in the approver's sole discretion, is final and binding, may be withdrawn if circumstances change, and a withheld approval must be kept confidential. Separately, the Board has designated a standing exception allowing employees to trade Long Term Incentive Plan awards that vest during a Blackout Period within 4 weeks of vesting to meet an immediate United States tax liability.
jurisdiction_overlays: United States tax law (exception for LTIP awards vesting during a Blackout Period that give rise to an immediate US tax liability)

bespoke_clauses.clause: Designated Persons must not engage in margin lending or other secured financing arrangements over Orora Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is a blanket, unconditional ban on the loan leg of a funded collar for Designated Persons (Directors, Senior Executives, all KMP and their Associates), with no clearance route and no carve-out for vested shares.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A disposal of Orora Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This exclusion contemplates a secured lender existing, yet Designated Persons are separately and absolutely banned from entering into any secured financing arrangement in the first place; it may only be relevant to non-Designated Orora Persons or legacy arrangements, and should not be read as reviving the loan leg for Designated Persons.

bespoke_clauses.clause: 'Derivatives' ... includes the following if they relate to or derive value from Orora Securities: ... contracts for difference, spread bets and caps and collars.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The Policy expressly anticipates a collar structure and treats it as a Derivative/Security, so the put/call legs are squarely Trading requiring notification (Designated Persons) and compliance with Blackout Periods, quite separate from the outright ban on the financing leg.

bespoke_clauses.clause: any hedging over vested Orora Securities must comply with this Policy and, if applicable to that Orora Person, Orora's Minimum Shareholding Policy
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar over vested shares subject to an MSR may be restricted or reduced in permitted size by the separate Minimum Shareholding Policy, which is not in this document and must be independently reviewed.

bespoke_clauses.clause: This prohibition against insider trading applies to all Orora Persons at all times, including outside of Blackout Periods and other ad hoc restriction periods, and overrides all other provisions of this Policy, including any consent or approval to trade which may be granted under this Policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even a Company Secretary/Chairman-approved collar trade cannot proceed, and any purported approval is void, if the executive possesses inside information at the time of execution.

bespoke_clauses.clause: it is unlikely that details of the ad hoc restriction will be communicated to all Orora Persons ... Any such communication is to be treated as confidential.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: An undisclosed ad hoc restriction can silently block execution or unwind of a collar even outside the scheduled Blackout Periods.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Following the end of each financial year, all Directors and Senior Executives must certify to the Company Secretary that they and their Associates are in compliance with this Policy (or advise of any breaches of this Policy).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar or loan arrangement inconsistent with the Policy would need to be disclosed (or falsely certified) at each annual compliance certification, so any secured financing question should be resolved with the Company Secretary well before that certification falls due.

summary: A funded collar over vested Orora shares faces a hard block on the loan leg: Designated Persons (Directors, Senior Executives, all KMP, and their Associates) 'must not engage in margin lending or other secured financing arrangements over Orora Securities', an unconditional ban with no clearance route. The derivative legs are, by contrast, expressly contemplated: 'Derivatives' is defined to include 'caps and collars' and other OTC instruments, and hedging of vested Orora Securities is permitted subject to compliance with the Policy (pre-trade notification for Designated Persons -- to the Chairman of the Board, the Chairman of the Audit & Compliance Committee, or the MD&CEO, as applicable, with a copy to the Company Secretary) and, if applicable, Orora's separate Minimum Shareholding Policy; hedging unvested securities under an employee plan is absolutely prohibited. Any dealing must also avoid the two annual Blackout Periods (31 December to half-year results; 30 June to full-year results) and any confidential ad hoc restriction, and can never proceed while the person holds inside information, which overrides any approval already granted. Outside those windows, only an exceptional-circumstances approval from the Company Secretary or Chairman (for severe hardship, a court order, or a circumstance the Chairman or Audit & Compliance Chair deems exceptional) permits a disposal during a Blackout Period. Overall verdict: the put/call collar structure itself is workable with notification outside Blackout Periods, but the bank's loan secured on the collared shares is expressly and unconditionally prohibited for Designated Persons, making a standard funded collar not achievable without restructuring the financing so that no security is taken over Orora shares.
